chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: Jam sessions after hours and who went out to play in the Moten band
summary: Jazz players went out to jam after work, as he did in Baltimore and Toledo. In the Moten band only he, Ben Webster and perhaps Eddie Durham did so.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I wanted to bring up another point.
The jam sessions seemed to be not only after the gigs but, you know, when somebody wanted to audition. They said, you know, play. AND THEY'D get together and jam.

Well, everybody, especially jazz players, I mean, you had a lot in those bands, the other guys in those bands, like in those days when you went in the band maybe you might be the only jazz man in there, especially in the section that you were in. But all the jazz men went out and played. Just like Roy Eldridge was one of the greatest jazz trumpet players of all times and he went out and played all the time. And this is how he and I went out together in Baltimore, Art Tatum and all the guys in Toledo that I was associated with, we went out at night after our respective jobs and played.
Well, the Moten band, they seemed to have a lot of jazz players in there?
Yeah, but in the Moten band the only guys that went out at night and played was Ben WEBSTER and

myself and possibly Eddie Durham. But the rest of the guys just would come in -- and lips (PHONETIC). But a lot of the guys would come out and listen, see. And guys went around looking for each other, you know. This is where we picked up our ideas. You take when Coleman Hawkins was living, every-time a new tenor player would come around that anybody was talking about, Coleman Hawkins would be there listening to him at night, see.
